title: An open cylinder with minimum material
stem: An open cylindrical container must hold 320 cubic centimetres. The base material costs twice as much per square centimetre as the side material. Let r be the radius and h the height, in centimetres. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Express the relative material cost in terms of r alone.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the radius and height minimising the cost.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Justify that the stationary value is the global minimum.

steps.text: Taking side cost as one unit per square centimetre, $C=2\pi r^2+2\pi rh=2\pi r^2+640/r$, $r>0$.
The cost is strictly convex; it also tends to infinity as r approaches zero or infinity, so this stationary point is the global minimum.

title: When logistic growth is fastest
stem: A population follows $P(t)=1000/(1+9e^{-0.4t})$, for $t\ge0$. It satisfies $P\prime=0.4P(1-P/1000)$. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find when this occurs and calculate the maximum growth rate.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain how the concavity changes at this time.

steps.text: Treat $P\prime=0.4P-0.0004P^2$ as a concave quadratic in P.
Maximum growth rate $=0.4(500)(1-0.5)=100$ individuals per time unit.
Before P=500 the growth rate is increasing, so the curve is concave up.
After P=500 the growth rate decreases, so the curve is concave down; the change gives an inflection point.
